svg.title: The three-plane model: what each plane is, how it is attacked, and why management plane loss is total
svg.desc: Three columns. Management plane: SSH, SNMP, syslog, NTP, TACACS - the plane that changes the device. Attacked by credential theft, weak passwords, exposed management addresses and insecure protocols. Controlled by out-of-band access, a management VRF, two factors, SSH only, SNMPv3 and command accounting. Losing it means the attacker owns the device completely. Control plane: routing protocols, ARP, STP, LACP, IGMP - the plane that decides where traffic goes. Attacked by forged adjacencies, floods that starve the CPU and protocol abuse. Controlled by CoPP, CPPr, rACL, authentication, TTL security and prefix limits. Losing it means traffic takes a path the attacker chose. Data plane: forwarding, ACLs, QoS, replication - the plane that moves packets. Attacked by spoofing, floods, VLAN hopping and table exhaustion. Controlled by uRPF, ACL placement, storm control, port security and segmentation. Bottom: an escalation ladder - data plane gives reach, control plane gives direction, management plane gives the device itself, and that is why management plane exposure is the only one that cannot be compensated for.
svg.text: Three planes, three different fights - and only one of them is unrecoverable
"Harden the device" means nothing until you say which plane, because the controls do not overlap.
MANAGEMENT PLANE
The plane that changes the device
SSH, SNMP, syslog, NTP, TACACS+
ATTACKED BY
stolen or default credentials
a management address reachable from the internet
telnet, SNMPv1/v2c, TFTP config pulls
CONTROLLED BY
out-of-band or management VRF
two factors, per-command accounting
SSH only, SNMPv3 authPriv, signed images
If this is lost, everything else is lost:
the attacker can change the ACLs that
were supposed to stop him.
CONTROL PLANE
The plane that decides direction
OSPF, BGP, IS-IS, ARP, STP, LACP
ATTACKED BY
forged hellos or updates with no authentication
floods that push the CPU to 100 percent
a route injection that black-holes a prefix
CONTROLLED BY
CoPP and CPPr with per-class rates
rACL / iACL, GTSM, protocol authentication
maximum prefix, route policy, BPDU guard
If this is lost, traffic still flows - but
along the path the attacker chose, and
the monitoring looks normal.
DATA PLANE
The plane that moves the packets
forwarding, ACLs, QoS, replication
ATTACKED BY
source address spoofing
VLAN hopping, MAC and table exhaustion
floods from a single compromised host
CONTROLLED BY
uRPF, ACL placement at the enforcement point
storm control, port security, private VLAN
segmentation so a host reaches only its peers
If this is lost, the blast radius is whatever
that segment can reach - which is exactly
what segmentation is meant to bound.
ESCALATION LADDER
data plane: reach - a foothold, one segment
control plane: direction - traffic, silently rerouted
management plane: the device itself
Only the third rung cannot be compensated for from elsewhere in the network: every other control is configured by the plane that is now under someone else's control.
That is why management plane hardening comes first in the priority list, even though it protects the asset nobody considers exciting.
